title: 2025-10-02-red-team-results-remediation-and-sdlc-patch-roadmap
summary: Review of red-team results from September engagement, triage of highest-severity findings, alignment on remediation windows and patch cadence, discussion of secure SDLC integrations, and next-steps to share detailed remediation plan and schedule follow-up validation/scan.
topics: Short-term remediation vs long-term SDLC fixes
Patch cadence and emergency change windows
Audit logs, KMS/encryption, RBAC and SSO integration
SOC 2 / ISO implications and evidence collection
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-02 15:00 PDT | Duration: 1:02:00 | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Sasha (CSM) ; Alex, Priya, Miguel, Lena (Aurora)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, we'll run through the red team findings and then walk through remediation options and the SDLC changes we recommended. is the timing still good on your side?
00:07 Alex: yeah good here, sorry for the late push, had a brief incident response sync first.
00:12 Derek: quick note, i'll be driving the technical bits — i'll reference the report numbers. the red team ran sept 18 to sept 22, you have the PDF link, right? (link shared in chat)
00:22 Priya: yes link is in the notes, we scanned the executive summary but want to get deeper into the handful of criticals.
00:28 Maya: perfect. quick agenda: top five items, owner/ETA, patch cadence alignment, and then how to bake fixes into your SDLC and CI gating.
00:36 Miguel: great. i'm most worried about the aws key exposure finding — we call it finding 01 in the report.
00:41 Derek: right so finding-01: service account keys found in a legacy S3 bucket snapshot. red team used it to spin up an instance and move laterally. CVSS 9.1 in our scoring, and there's a clear path to privilege escalation because the instance role had overly broad iam perms.
00:57 Priya: we had a temporary mitigation already — rotated keys last week — but lane, excuse me, lena will need to collect proof for SOC-2. what artifacts do you recommend?
01:06 Sasha: for SOC 2 evidence you'll want the key rotation logs, KMS access events if applicable, and the audit trail showing the bucket object access. Derek, do we have an artifact checklist?
01:15 Derek: yes i'll send the checklist. long-story-short: rotation event timestamps, cloudtrail logs for the object GET and PUT, and we recommend retaining the pre-rotation access logs in a tamper-evident store for review. note: cloudtrail sometimes shows service names as 'Kay V cache' in our transcript — ha — but the log fields are ok.
01:31 Miguel: okay. second item, finding-03 was a weak session-handling issue in the API, we saw session fixation in the puppet harness.
01:40 Derek: yep that one maps to CWE-384-ish, and the fix is changing cookie attributes and rotating session tokens on privilege changes plus a short token TTL. low-risk code change but needs regression tests.
01:51 Alex: timeline question: what's realistic for high/critical fix deployment vs lower priority? we have fortnightly sprint releases and a monthly maintenance window.
02:01 Maya: good question. for high/critical (9+ cvss) we typically recommend emergency change for immediate patching — short patch window + hotfix followed by a formal PR into main. ripple to your change freeze/maintenance windows?
02:12 Miguel: our ops change window is 03:00-05:00 UTC on Sundays; emergency changes outside that require CAB approval but we can expedite for criticals.
02:20 Priya: for compliance we need to capture the risk acceptance or emergency CAB notes too. the SOC-2 auditor will want to see decision records.
02:29 Derek: agreed. we'll include a remediation timeline template you can put in JIRA and a sample CAB record.
02:35 Lena: about encryption — finding-04 flagged weak key rotation policies for TLS certs and some services not using customer-managed KMS. what's best practice for a mixed cloud/on-prem set up?
02:46 Derek: best practice: customer-managed keys for all sensitive data at rest where you manage lifecycle via KMS, and rotate per your org policy. for TLS certs we recommend automated renewal (e.g., cert-manager) and private PKI for internal services. also ensure HSM-backed KMS for keys used for credential sealing.
03:01 Priya: do you support evidence of HSM usage in the private deployment docs?
03:04 Maya: yes we have a Private deployment checklist that documents KMS/HSM integrations, key wrapping, and key rotation proofs — we'll share the doc.
03:11 Alex: another big one — RBAC misconfig in the data platform. finding-07 said dev role had db:delete permissions. how are you recommending role scoping?
03:20 Derek: principle of least privilege is the baseline. we recommend role templates in terraform, org-level policies limiting write/delete to a small set of service accounts, and regular IAM attestation reviews — quarterly. automated attestation is ideal: list of role owners in a table and a signed attestation event.
03:35 Miguel: feasible. we have some legacy services that assume ownerless perms. we'll schedule work to adopt the templates.
03:40 Priya: on SSO — the report noted a couple of service accounts not bound to SSO (okta) and still using static creds. is there a recommended migration path?
03:48 Derek: migrate service accounts to OIDC where possible, adopt short-lived tokens (vault or sts), and put the long-lived creds in a vault with rotation. Okta for human SSO, OIDC for machine identities. we have a migration playbook for that.
04:02 Alex: we also had a callout about audit logs: retention, tamper-evidence, and partitioning by region for data residency. Aurora has eu residency requirements for buckets storing euro PII.
04:14 Maya: yes important. for data residency keep logs in the region where the event originated, or replicate read-only archives to a secure compliance region, and provide proof of location to auditors. for tamper evidence, S3 object lock or write-once policies plus KMS key separation help.
04:29 Lena: do you recommend a single KMS per region or a centralized key management with geo restrictions?
04:34 Derek: depends. single KMS per region simplifies residency and audit. centralized KMS can work but you need strict network controls and legal review because key export across borders can be sensitive.
04:47 Priya: SOC 2 question: will the remediation plan and attestation artifacts be enough for our Type 2 scope?
04:54 Maya: yes, as long as you maintain evidence of patching, change approvals, and log collection. we'll provide a mapping doc between each finding and the SOC 2 control (minimal mapping example included in the deck).
05:05 Miguel: about patch cadence — we currently run monthly package updates in a pre-prod window and quarterly reboots for infra. the red team suggested quicker cadence for public-facing services. what's best?
05:16 Derek: try a 2-week security patch lane for internet-facing services, monthly for internal, and quarterly for low-risk infra. build canary PRs, automated smoke tests, and live rollback hooks. that reduces exposure window for known CVEs.
05:29 Alex: does that create a lot of operational overhead?
05:31 Derek: some, but automation reduces the human cost. Redwood's recommendations include a daily CVE watch, automated image rebuilds, and a canary deployment to 5% of traffic.
05:42 Priya: can Redwood run an independent re-scan after we mark items fixed?
05:46 Maya: yes we offer verification scans and a re-assessment package. we'll schedule the re-scan after you push hotfixes — typically 2 weeks after remediation to validate.
05:55 Lena: are there any quick wins we can do in the next sprint?
05:58 Derek: top quick wins: rotate exposed keys (done), enforce http-only and secure cookie flags, reduce token TTLs for sessions, apply terraform role templates to block delete ops, and move service creds into vault.
06:12 Miguel: can you prioritize which of those should be in sprint-1?
06:15 Maya: we suggest sprint-1: key rotation verification, cookie/session fixes, and vaulting service creds. sprint-2: role templates and canary/automation. sprint-3: certificate automation and HSM rollout.
06:26 Priya: timeline acceptable. for evidence collection, what's the output artifact list?
06:29 Sasha: our deliverables: remediation plan with PR links, CAB records, change logs, cloudtrail + KMS audit snapshots, proof-of-fix screenshots and re-scan report. we'll also provide a compliance mapping doc to SOC 2 controls.
06:43 Alex: good. a few clarifying Qs — about the CVE references in the report, one item referenced CVE-2025-1024 but it seemed like a library issue — do you have the line-of-sight?
06:53 Derek: yes that one was an upstream lib with a patched release last month. mitigation: bump the dependency and rebuild images; we included the exact commit and PR in the appendix.
07:03 Priya: run-book integration — can we get sample runbook snippets for incident response aligned with the red-team scenarios?
07:09 Maya: yes, we'll include runbook snippets and a recommended on-call escalation path.
07:14 Alex: OK let's cover next steps.
07:16 Maya: recap: we'll email detailed remediation plan and artifact checklist by end of day tomorrow, include a CAB template and SOC 2 mapping. Derek will send the technical checklist and the playbook for OIDC migration. Sasha will coordinate scheduling the verification re-scan for two weeks after fixes.
07:31 Miguel: and we'll target sprint-1 items for the release on 2025-10-12.
07:36 Priya: thanks everyone. one last ask — can you include a sample attestations spreadsheet for quarterly IAM attestation?
07:43 Derek: yes, sending sample CSV.
07:45 Maya: cool, we'll follow up via email and JIRA. thanks all.
07:49 (meeting ends)
next_steps: Redwood to send remediation plan + artifact checklist by 2025-10-03
Derek to share technical checklist and OIDC migration playbook (link) by 2025-10-03
Schedule verification re-scan two weeks after fixes (Sasha to coordinate)
Aurora to target sprint-1 release for quick wins on 2025-10-12
Redwood to provide SOC 2 mapping doc and CAB template

Derek Huang - Share technical checklist, OIDC migration playbook, and sample attestations CSV by 2025-10-03
Sasha Rivera - Coordinate verification re-scan and schedule with Aurora by 2025-10-20
Miguel Ortiz - Implement sprint-1 fixes (rotate keys, cookie/session changes, vault creds) targeted 2025-10-12
